Clerk pricing matrix: "Passkeys — Authenticate with any form of passkeys": not included on the Free plan, included on Pro and above; "Biometric sign-in — Let returning users sign in to native apps with their device's biometrics" is likewise a paid-tier feature.

Clerk site: "Bot Detection — Dramatically reduce fraudulent sign-ups with built-in, continually updated machine learning" and "Email and SMS one-time passcodes — Fast and reliable one-time passcode delivery with built-in brute force prevention."

Clerk site, Session Management: "Clerk manages the full session lifecycle, including critical security functionality like active device monitoring and session revocation" — with per-device sign-out ("Sign out of device") shown in the user profile UI.

Clerk pricing: the Free plan carries a "Machine Authentication — API Keys & M2M Tokens limit per month"; machine authentication (API keys and machine-to-machine tokens) is a metered platform feature across plans.

Says Clerk is 'a mess': its libraries pull in everything (Web3, Stripe), and the JS blob triggers browser slow-load warnings. On every React upgrade, Clerk libraries were the biggest pain because of transitive dependencies, including conflicting Stripe library versions. Also says the libraries are obfuscated and the 'isomorphic' TS code is an impenetrable mess to debug.

Complains the Clerk platform lacks audit logs and versioning. Someone changed a setting in the console and the team couldn't trace when it happened or who did it. Also had to get up on a Sunday because Clerk API calls for token refreshes were failing.

Clerk 'looks really good initially' and is 'perfect if you want to prototype something and not care about auth,' but the details hurt. There's still no offline auth on mobile, so the app can't open without connectivity. Says auth must always work 'and Clerk just fails this test'; switching the company to Logto.

Workaround for offline mobile auth: cached the credentials and Clerk's JWT refresh token, then manually requested access tokens via Clerk's 'sparsely documented frontend API'. This required faking the cache API and plucking the token from the undocumented '__clerk_client_jwt' key. Says Better Auth supports this out of the box.

Using Clerk and 'quite unhappy with it'. No proper RBAC: roles are tied to organizations, not stored on the user, so there's no global admin concept unless you put arbitrary key-value pairs in metadata. More than once in recent weeks/months a Clerk downtime made the whole app fail. 'Would think twice before using it in the future.'
Feels Clerk adoption has become the norm in recent years. Started using it about a year ago and found it to have troublesome reliability.

Recently switched from Clerk to BetterAuth: it supports more of what they need, is more reliable, and is much cheaper. Originally picked Clerk because there was no open-source alternative and they wouldn't roll their own auth. Now sees no reason to pick Clerk, Auth0 or Kinde.
Prefers Better Auth because it's 'way more hackable than using something like Clerk'. They added a plugin to allow auth via iframe postMessage (embedded in a CRM) and it worked seamlessly.
With Better Auth you get your auth data in your own DB and many OAuth providers for free. 'Not saying Supabase and Clerk are bad, but they cost money.'
Glad they chose WorkOS and have been a happy camper there. Had wondered about Clerk because it felt hotter: 'Turns out hot isn't always good.'
Warns against outsourcing auth to VC-funded vendors that will eventually 'milk you dry'. Adds: 'Clerk's pricing should be evidence enough.'

Recently picked a vendor whose agentic observability product is built on Supabase + Clerk and found a staggering number of vulnerabilities and CVEs from that stack. Advises being wary of vendors built on Supabase + Clerk.
'Clerk seems fine, Auth0 is fine, but I'd rather build on open-source.'
'I think Clerk looks great but it starts to get quite expensive if MFA is a requirement.'
'Really good stuff. The Next.js integration story is already really quite good.' Appreciates a service that takes away all the pain of user management, not just login.

Confused by Clerk's pricing: free up to 5,000 MAU, but the paid tier is $49/mo for 1,000 MAU plus $0.05 per additional MAU. So going from 5,000 to 5,001 MAU jumps from $0 to $249/mo. Also unclear how MAU is calculated.

Since Clerk lists security as a top-level feature, notes poor security-header scores for clerk.dev and the dashboard. Calls it a red flag that the dashboard and customer logins load third-party CDN JS (jsdelivr) without SRI.

Hesitant to trust even Auth0 with user management, so asks why they'd trust a new company like Clerk. Another commenter worries the service could go under within a year, forcing a migration to Cognito or Okta.
